questions.q: In the plate-stack analogy from this lesson, why can you only remove a plate from the top of the stack?
options: The stack is a Last-In-First-Out (LIFO) structure, just like the EVM's own stack
It's just a random rule with no real computer-science meaning
Plates in the middle are made of a different material
The EVM doesn't actually use a stack at all
questions.explain: The EVM's stack is LIFO — the last value pushed on is the first one popped off, exactly like only being able to remove the top plate from a stack.

questions.q: How many items can the EVM's stack hold, and how wide is each one?
options: Up to 1,024 items, each 256 bits wide
Unlimited items of any size
Exactly 10 items, each 8 bits wide
1 item at a time
questions.explain: The EVM's stack holds up to 1,024 items, each 256 bits wide — a real, fixed constraint of the virtual machine.

questions.q: What is an opcode, per the real evm.codes reference shown in this lesson?
options: A single, literal EVM instruction — like ADD or STOP — each with its own gas cost
A type of Solidity variable
A synonym for a smart contract's address
A Remix-specific feature with no relation to the EVM itself
questions.explain: Opcodes are the real, literal instruction set the EVM executes — every Solidity contract ultimately breaks down into a sequence of these.

questions.q: Why does a more complex smart contract cost more gas, per this lesson?
options: It executes more opcodes, and every opcode has its own real gas cost
Complex contracts are taxed at a higher fixed rate
Gas cost has nothing to do with contract complexity
Complexity only affects deployment time, never cost
questions.explain: Every operation your contract performs is an opcode with its own cost — the more operations (the more complex the contract), the more total gas it costs.

questions.q: Why does EVM-compatibility matter for moving a project between blockchains?
options: EVM-compatible chains (like Polygon or Avalanche) can run the same bytecode Ethereum's EVM runs, easing migration
It has no practical benefit at all
Only Ethereum itself can ever run Solidity contracts
EVM-compatibility only affects gas token names, not code portability
questions.explain: Because Solidity compiles to the same EVM instruction set, EVM-compatible chains can run the same contracts with minimal changes, letting projects move to wherever their users are.
